chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Safwan, from Umar ibn Rabah, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'When I arrive in Mecca, do I complete the prayer or shorten it?' He said, 'Complete it.' I said, 'And when I pass through Medina, do I complete the prayer or shorten it?' He said, 'Complete it.'
ai.seo_question: Do travelers shorten their prayers when visiting Mecca or Medina?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific jurisprudential status of Mecca and Medina as 'cities of residence' (madinat al-) for travelers, overriding the general rule of shortening prayers (qasr). The Imam’s directive to perform full four-rak'ah prayers in both locations underscores their unique sanctity and legal standing in Shia fiqh, distinguishing them from other travel destinations. This ruling is foundational for understanding the conditions under which the traveler's prayer is considered complete rather than shortened.
